newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African Masterbond 40 mln rand settlement agreed.
newsitem.headline: S.African Masterbond 40 mln rand settlement agreed.

text.p: Ernst & Young, statutory auditors to failed investment firm Masterbond, said on Wednesday that agreement had been reached with the curators of Masterbond to settle all claims against the company.
This would see a 40.25 million rand fund set up by Masterbond and Ernst & Young and the distribution of those funds by a receiver appointed by the Cape Town Supreme Court.
Masterbond collapsed last year after three of its directors were found guilty in October 1995 of seven counts of fraud involving 129 million rand.

"We are pleased to advise that the firm, in conjunction with the previous auditors of Masterbond, has reached agreement in principle with Masterbond's curators in regard to a settlement of all alleged claims against the firm," Ernst & Young said.
The settlement arrangement requires the approval of the court and 75 percent of Masterbond investors.
The court application authorising the convening of meetings of creditors will begin immediately, Ernst & Young said.

"If approved the arrangement, which is made without admission of liability, will resolve all potential claims by the Masterbond group and investors and will avoid the possibility of years of expensive and disruptive litigation," Ernst & Young said.
The criminal activities of the Masterbond trio left many elderly people and pensioners in dire financial straits.
One pensioner committed suicide after the Masterbond crash and another testified that she had lost all her money and was now dependent on the state.
